A spreadsheet, or a tool built for the shop? An honest comparison.

The spreadsheet wins more than people admit. It’s free, it’s already open, and the owner built every column. For a lot of small businesses it’s the right tool.

Where it starts to cost: one file, and whoever saved last wins. The quote gets retyped into the invoice. A formula breaks and nobody notices until month end.

Off-the-shelf software makes you learn its words. A spreadsheet makes you build it yourself. Waypoint builds the software around how a business already works.

What they said: “No rush. Whenever you get a chance.”

A contact form, or a request form that routes the job?

The contact form: name, email, a message box. “Hi, need a quote, call me.” Then someone calls back, asks for the address and photos, and types it into the schedule.

A request form asks for the address, the job type, photos and the best time up front, in the business’s own words, and lands on the right person’s schedule with the address already on it.

Where the contact form wins: ten minutes to set up and nothing to explain. If you get three messages a month, keep it. If you get more, Waypoint builds the request side around how you dispatch today.

Nova Scotia short-term rental hosts: a quick registration check.

Places rented for 28 days in a row or less must be registered with the province’s Short-term Rentals Registry, and the registration number has to appear on booking-platform listings. Registrations renew every year by April 1. Fines for not registering can reach $100,000 CAD for each year.

Source: Government of Nova Scotia, Register your short-term accommodation: https://www.novascotia.ca/register-your-short-term-accommodation
